title: Arroz de Pato
subtitle: Portuguese baked duck rice
excerpt: One of Portugal's great rice dishes: a whole duck or duck legs braised in white wine and aromatics, the cooking liquor used to cook the rice with chorizo and olives, the shredded duck meat folded through, and the whole thing baked until the top is golden.

recipe.sourceNotes: Arroz de pato (duck rice) is one of the most celebrated dishes in Portuguese cooking, associated particularly with the Braga region in the north. It belongs to the tradition of 'rice of' dishes common in Portugal, where the cooking liquid of a meat or fish is used to cook rice, producing a result more flavoured than any plain rice can achieve. The duck is braised first until tender; the rich broth from the braise is then used to cook short-grain rice with smoked chorizo and olives. The shredded duck is folded through, the whole thing spread in a wide baking dish, and baked until the top is golden and slightly crispy. In Portugal it is often served at celebrations and family gatherings.

content.text: The broth from braising the duck is the key to the flavour of the rice; skim the fat from the surface before using it and season it well. Measure the broth carefully: you need exactly twice the volume of rice in liquid. The rice will finish cooking in the oven, so undercook it slightly on the hob.

Put the duck legs in a large pot with the onion, carrot, garlic, bay leaves, thyme, peppercorns, wine, and enough water to cover by 4 cm. Bring to a simmer, skimming the surface. Cook gently for 1 hour 15 minutes until the duck is very tender. Lift out the duck; strain and reserve the broth. When cool enough to handle, shred the duck meat from the bones; discard the skin if you prefer.

Heat the oven to 200°C / fan 180°C / gas 6. Skim the fat from the broth. Measure 600 ml of broth and bring to a boil in a saucepan. Add the rice and cook for 10 minutes, stirring; it should be partially cooked but still firm. Stir in the chorizo, olives, and shredded duck meat. Season with salt.

Transfer to a buttered wide baking dish and spread evenly. Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until the top is golden and slightly crisp. The rice should be cooked through with a little caramelisation at the edges. Serve straight from the dish.
